signal.title: CPNav: Calibrated Vision-Language Navigation for Object-Goal Search in Unseen Environments
signal.summary: 这项研究聚焦机器人在动态或开放环境中的运动规划，尝试让路径不仅能到达目标，也能满足安全和物理约束。

editorial.intro: 这项研究聚焦机器人在动态或开放环境中的运动规划，尝试让路径不仅能到达目标，也能满足安全和物理约束。
editorial.why_it_matters: 运动规划连接感知、世界模型和执行控制，是具身智能从算法演示走向可靠运行的关键环节。
editorial.watch_next: 继续核对复杂场景、碰撞率和真实机器人上的执行效果。

evidence.title: CPNav: Calibrated Vision-Language Navigation for Object-Goal Search in Unseen Environments
evidence.excerpt: Directing a robot to locate a target object in unseen environments remains a central challenge in embodied AI. Vision-Language Model (VLM)-based methods provide rich semantic reasoning but often produce uncalibrated and overconfident action decisions. We introduce CPNav, a navigation framework that combines collision-aware planning with statistically calibrated VLM action scoring for map-free object-goal navigation. From RGB-D input, CPNav constructs a navigability map, generates collision-free motion primitives, and queries two VLMs for goal detection and action scoring. The resulting scores are calibrated offline via conformal prediction (CP) using oracle actions obtained through a tree-structured exploration procedure with backtracking, providing finite-sample guarantees at a user-specified risk level. The CP layer is model-agnostic and can wrap any VLM policy. Online, calibrated VLM scores guide action selection, while a tree-structured exploration history records alternative actions and allows backtracking. We evaluate CPNav in both simulation and real-world hardware settings. In AI Habitat simulation, compared with the uncalibrated baseline method, CPNav achieves relative SR
